useCase.name: Create an exam, schedule its papers, and publish the timetable once approved

intent.name: exam.create
intent.summary: Create an exam and fix each subject's total, passing and grace marks in the same act. Two steps, and the three figures can never be changed afterwards.

routesHere.gloss: create the First Term exam, starting 12 November

routesHere.gloss: we need to create a new exam — for classes 6, 7 and 8

routesHere.gloss: set the total and passing marks for each subject too

routesHere: set up the mid-term exam with theory out of 70 and practical out of 30

request.text: paper ki tareekh rakh do
request.gloss: set the paper's date

routesElsewhere.note: Creating the exam fixes what is examined and how it is marked. When each paper is sat is scheduled separately.

request.text: total marks badal do
request.gloss: change the total marks

routesElsewhere.note: The total, passing and grace figures are fixed at creation and cannot be changed afterwards (BR-3). Marks entry and grade calculation both read them, and a rule that moves after marks are entered makes every earlier entry unexplainable.

request.text: imtihan ka natija nikalo
request.gloss: produce the exam result

routesElsewhere.note: Creating an exam produces no marks and no results. It schedules an exam; it examines nobody (BR-11).

request.text: purana exam mita do
request.gloss: delete the old exam

routesElsewhere.note: An exam is never deleted. One that will not run is cancelled, and its schedule and approvals stay readable (BR-12).

steps.note: The exam and what it covers. A subject not attached to the class cannot be examined in it (BR-1).

Every subject carries its own total, passing and grace figures (BR-2) — a single figure across an exam does not survive contact with a practical paper worth 30 and a theory paper worth 70. Fixed here for good (BR-3).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Where step 2 fails the exam exists in Draft with no subject rules, and the rules are set again rather than the exam created twice.
plan.atomicity: Not atomic across the two steps. Step 1 writes the exam and step 2 the marking rules, and an exam left without rules is visible in Draft and can be completed. Nothing is published, nobody is notified and no student is examined by either step (BR-11).

parameters.notes: Unique within the academic session (E1). Where the actor did not give one, ask — never derive it from the name.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.notes: Not in the past, and a working day.

parameters.name: class_subjects
parameters.notes: The classes examined and, per class, the subjects. A subject not attached to the class cannot be examined in it (BR-1). Named by the actor; never widened to "all subjects" on their behalf.

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.description: Draft. Nothing is scheduled, approved or published yet.

operations.idempotencyKey: exam_id + subject_id, since a subject carries one set of rules
operations.purpose: Fix the total marks, passing marks and maximum grace for each subject in the exam.

parameters.name: exam_id
parameters.notes: The exam created in step 1.

parameters.name: subject_rules
parameters.notes: Per subject: total marks, passing marks and maximum grace marks (BR-2). Every figure is the actor's; a planner that supplies a customary 100 and 40 is inventing the school's marking scheme.

fields.name: rules
fields.description: Per subject, the three figures now fixed (BR-3).

fields.name: subjects_without_rules
fields.description: Subjects in the exam still carrying no rules. The exam cannot be submitted for approval until every one has them.

errors.meaning: The passing marks are not below the total.
errors.notWritten: No rules saved for that subject.
errors.note: The message names the subject and both figures (BR-2).

errors.meaning: The three figures already exist for that subject and a change was attempted.
errors.note: Fixed at creation and not changeable afterwards (BR-3). Report it; there is no route past it.

planningRules.rule: Never supply a total, passing or grace figure the actor did not state. They are fixed for the life of the exam (BR-3) and every mark and grade is read against them — a figure a planner assumed becomes the school's marking scheme.
Never plan a change to those three figures. E3 is BR-3 working, and an exam whose rules moved after marks were entered makes every earlier entry unexplainable.

Never widen the classes or subjects. "The exam" means the classes and subjects the actor named; a planner that reads it as every class in the school schedules papers for children who were not being examined.
Report the subjects rejected for not being attached to the class. They are silently absent from the exam otherwise, and nobody discovers it until the timetable is read (BR-1).
Never describe the exam as scheduled or published. Creating one produces no marks and no results, and nothing is visible to anybody until it is approved and published (BR-11, BR-6).

Ask for the code rather than deriving one. It is unique within the session (E1) and appears on every result — a planner that builds "FT-2026" from the exam's name has named the school's records for it.
session_id and branch_id come from $session, even where the request names a year or a campus.

reversal.statement: An exam is never deleted (BR-12). One created in error is cancelled with a reason, which keeps its schedule and approvals readable. The controller must not attempt a compensating call after a failed step 2 — the exam stands in Draft and its rules are set again.

operations.name: exam.paper.schedule
operations.idempotencyKey: exam_id + subject_id, since a subject carries one slot
operations.purpose: Schedule one paper with its date, slot, duration, invigilator and marks deadline.

parameters.name: exam_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No exam matches within the actor's scope for this session.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with their code, dates and status.

parameters.notes: The exam, resolved from its name or code.

parameters.name: subject_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. That subject is not in this exam.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the subjects in the exam and their classes.

parameters.notes: The subject within the exam, which fixes the class the paper is for.

parameters.name: paper_date
parameters.notes: The day the paper is sat. Not a day the school is closed (BR-10, E4).

parameters.name: time_slot
parameters.notes: The start time, 24-hour. Two papers for the same class must not overlap (BR-10, E5).

parameters.name: duration_minutes
parameters.notes: How long the paper runs. The actor's; never taken from another paper.

parameters.name: marks_deadline
parameters.notes: When the subject's teacher must have uploaded the marks. On or after the paper date (BR-5, E6). It is what makes the completeness check in marks entry mean anything.

parameters.name: invigilator_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No staff member matches within the actor's scope.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with their subject and class.

parameters.notes: The staff member invigilating. A clash with their own timetable is not checked by anything modelled here.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: marks_deadline
fields.description: The teacher's deadline for this subject (BR-5).

fields.name: subjects_unscheduled
fields.description: Subjects in the exam still carrying no slot.

errors.meaning: The date is a holiday or an off-day.
errors.note: The message names the day and why it is closed. Choose another date with the Coordinator; never move the calendar to fit the paper.

errors.meaning: Another paper for the same class overlaps that slot.
errors.note: The message names the other paper. A class cannot sit two papers at once (BR-10).

errors.meaning: The marks deadline falls before the paper date.

planningRules.rule: Never choose a date or a time the actor did not give. A timetable is read by every family in the school, and a planner that filled in "the next working day" has scheduled an exam nobody agreed to.
Never work around a closed day or a clash. E4 and E5 are BR-10 working — report which day is closed or which paper clashes, and let the Coordinator choose another slot.
Never derive the marks deadline from the paper date. It is the teacher's deadline and the completeness check reads it (BR-5); a planner that added a customary week set that teacher's workload.
Report the subjects still unscheduled. Every paper needs a slot before the exam can go for approval, and the Coordinator discovers it at submission otherwise.
Never describe the schedule as published. Students, families and teachers learn nothing until the School Admin approves it (BR-6, BR-7).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: No reversal is offered. A slot is rescheduled while the exam is in Draft; once published, a change is the School Admin's and carries a reason (BR-9).

operations.name: exam.approve
operations.idempotencyKey: exam_id, since an exam is approved once and a repeat must not notify every family twice
operations.purpose: Approve the exam and publish its schedule to everybody concerned.

parameters.name: exam_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No exam matches within the actor's scope for this session.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with their code, dates and status.

parameters.notes: The exam awaiting approval.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: papers_published
fields.description: Each paper with its date, slot and duration, as families now see it.

fields.name: teachers_notified
fields.description: Each told their own invigilation, their own marking and their own deadline (BR-8).

fields.description: Delivery status per the Messaging module policy.

errors.meaning: The actor is the Coordinator who created the exam.
errors.note: The Coordinator creates and schedules; the School Admin approves (BR-6).

errors.meaning: The exam is in Draft, Returned, Published or Cancelled.
errors.note: Publication before approval is refused (BR-6). Report the state it is actually in.

planningRules.rule: Never chain a separate publication call. Approval publishes the schedule in the same act (BR-7), and a second call would message every family in the exam twice.
Never approve an exam the actor created. E8 is BR-6 working, and a planner that reached for approval on a Coordinator's behalf would collapse the only check on a timetable.
Report what was published and to whom. This is the moment thousands of families are messaged, and "approved" alone does not say that it happened.
Never re-approve to resend a notification. The approval is idempotent for good reason; a resend is not a plan this contract offers.

Never plan a change to the schedule in the same breath. Once published, a change is an edit that carries a reason and notifies everybody again (BR-9) — moving a date one minute after publishing it messages every family twice for one decision.

reversal.statement: An approval is not withdrawn. A published schedule is edited with a reason and everybody affected is notified (BR-9); an exam that will not run at all is cancelled (BR-12). The controller must not attempt a compensating call — the notifications have already gone.

operations.name: exam.return
operations.idempotencyKey: exam_id, since an exam sits in one place at a time
operations.purpose: Return the exam to the Coordinator with the reason it was not approved.

parameters.name: exam_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No exam matches within the actor's scope for this session.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with their code, dates and status.

parameters.notes: The exam awaiting approval.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 500 characters. Why it was not approved. The Coordinator acts on it, so it says what to change.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Returned. It sits with the Coordinator again.

errors.meaning: A return was recorded with no reason.
errors.note: Ask what should change; never compose one.

errors.meaning: The exam is not awaiting approval.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the reason. The Coordinator acts on it, and a reason a planner wrote sends somebody rescheduling papers on a guess.
Never notify students or families of a return. Nothing was published to them, and telling them an exam was not approved would be the first they had heard of it (A3).
Never plan the correction alongside the return. What to change is the Coordinator's to decide from the reason given.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A return is not withdrawn. The Coordinator corrects the exam and resubmits it, which is the route back.

steps.note: One step, and it messages every affected teacher, student and guardian. A changed date nobody was told about is worse than no schedule at all (BR-9).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A change with no reason, a closed day and a clash all arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the changed slots, the reason and the notifications to every affected teacher, student and guardian together or not at all (BR-9). What marks already entered against a moved paper become is not specified anywhere in this use case — it is an open question, and a Coordinator moving a paper that has been sat should be told so.

operations.name: exam.schedule.edit
operations.idempotencyKey: exam_id + changes, since a repeat must not message every family twice
operations.purpose: Change one or more papers in a published schedule, with the reason, notifying everybody affected.

parameters.name: exam_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No exam matches within the actor's scope for this session.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with their code, dates and status.

parameters.notes: The published exam.

parameters.name: changes
parameters.notes: Per paper: the subject and the new date, slot, duration, deadline or invigilator. Only what the actor named — a planner that tidied the rest of the timetable moved papers nobody asked about.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 500 characters. Required (BR-9, E10). It goes to every family told of the change, so it is the school's own words.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The change and who was told.

fields.name: papers_changed
fields.description: Each paper with its previous and new slot.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: As given, sent to everybody affected.

fields.name: teachers_notified
fields.description: Affected teachers told, with their duties restated (BR-8).

fields.name: marks_already_entered
fields.description: Papers changed that already carry marks. What becomes of them is not specified (open question).

errors.meaning: A published schedule was edited with no reason.
A new date is a holiday or an off-day.
A new slot overlaps another paper for the same class.
errors.note: The message names the other paper.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the reason. It goes to every family told of the change (BR-9), and a reason a planner wrote is the school explaining itself in words nobody chose.
Change only the papers the actor named. Every change messages families, and a planner that tidied an adjacent slot has told a hundred households their child's exam moved.
Report where a changed paper already carries marks. What becomes of them is not specified anywhere in this use case, and moving a paper that has been sat is the moment to say so rather than after.
Never work around a closed day or a clash on an edit. The same checks apply as at scheduling (BR-10), and a published timetable is a worse place to break them.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: No reversal is offered. A change put back is another edit, with its own reason, and everybody is messaged again. The controller must not attempt a compensating call — the first notifications have gone.

intent.summary: Cancel an exam that will not run, with the reason, keeping its schedule and approvals readable. One step.
routesHere: cancel the mid-term exam — the school is closed that week

routesElsewhere.note: Cancelling ends the whole exam. Removing or moving one paper is an edit to the schedule.

request.text: record se hata do
request.gloss: remove it from the records

routesElsewhere.note: An exam is never deleted. Its schedule and approvals stay readable after cancellation (BR-12).

steps.note: One step. It is cancelled rather than deleted, everybody concerned is notified, and its schedule and approvals stay readable (BR-12, A6).

plan.atomicity: One write: the cancellation, its reason, and the notifications to everybody who was told of the schedule, together or not at all. Nothing is erased — the papers, the slots, the duties and the approvals stay readable, because a school has to be able to say what it had planned and why it did not happen (BR-12).

operations.name: exam.cancel
operations.idempotencyKey: exam_id, since an exam is cancelled once and a repeat must not notify everybody twice
operations.purpose: Cancel an exam, keeping its schedule and approvals readable.

parameters.name: exam_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No exam matches within the actor's scope for this session.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with their code, dates and status.

parameters.notes: The exam being cancelled.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 500 characters. Why the exam will not run. It goes to everybody who was told of the schedule.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Cancelled. Terminal, and its record stays readable (BR-12).

fields.name: papers_cancelled
fields.description: The papers that will not now be sat, with their scheduled slots kept.

fields.name: marks_already_entered
fields.description: Papers already carrying marks. They are kept and not erased.

fields.name: recipients_notified
fields.description: Everybody who had been told the schedule.

planningRules.rule: Never describe cancellation as deletion. An exam is never deleted, and its schedule and approvals stay readable afterwards (BR-12) — a family asking why their child's exam did not happen is owed a record.
Never compose the reason. It goes to every family that was told of the schedule.
Report where marks were already entered. They are kept, not erased, and whoever entered them should know the exam they belong to has been cancelled.
Never cancel to fix a mistake in the schedule. A wrong date is an edit (BR-9); cancelling tells every family the exam is off.
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: Cancelled is terminal. An exam that runs after all is created afresh, which is deliberate — everybody was told this one was off.
